An estimation of the $B^0_s\rightarrow K^+K^-$ decay time for $B^0_s$ mesons has been made with the help of around 37 picobarns of LHCb data from 2010. This measure allows for constraints on theories beyond the Standard Model that may influence the $B^0_s$ system and was found to be 1.440 picoseconds by employing two methods with varying degrees of uncertainty, specifically 0.096 (statistical) ± 0.008 (systematic) ± 0.003 (model-based).

This research paper focuses on the numerical solution of a stochastic control problem governed by a parabolic equation with the control variable affecting the diffusion coefficient, particularly with the presence of rough inputs; it establishes the convergence of a specific numerical discretization method and provides an alternative solution using a stochastic simulation technique known as the Monte-Carlo method.

Our in-depth examination of extremely energetic cosmic rays detected at the Pierre Auger Observatory allows the detection of significant anisotropies at large scales, exceeding 75 degrees in extent, for particles with energies surpassing 4 EeV. The observed patterns of anisotropy are aligned with the Galactic plane and the Cosmic Microwave Background's inherent temperature and polarization gradients, suggesting a component of extremely directional anisotropy. The observed anisotropies are highly consistent with the patterns generated by extensive cosmic simulations, which account for the interactions of extremely energetic cosmic rays with the cosmic microwave background and the Galaxy, and support the hypothesis that cosmic accelerators are situated within galaxy clusters and groups. The absence of anisotropies related to the CMB's inherent gradient in the direction of the Local Group is also noted. The findings are highly dependent on the results of accurate local and global cosmic simulations and are subject to change with the expansion of the Kilo-Degree Survey and future cosmic-ray maps from satellites.

This paper proves that any finite-dimensional Zinbiel algebra over a given field has a specific characteristic - commutativity. Additionally, if the algebra's base field does not contain two, any field characteristics, it must be able to differentiate between its elements and arrays, then it will have a particular dimension - aligning with the dimensions of a specific type of array called the Malinai operators.

This study provides first-time data on the fluctuations of a specific angle, known as $\Psi_n$, and magnitude, known as $v_n$, related to particle flow, which have been determined using a newly developed technique for four-particle correlations. Researchers used ALICE to collect these data in high-energy Pb-Pb collisions at the LHC. Fluctuations in both angle and magnitude were found to increase with particle multiplicity and were similar in behavior for different harmonic numbers (even and odd). Additionally, a comparison with theoretical predictions from the MONES and iEPOS models showed that the results could be influenced by initial conditions and hadronization, and also reflected similarities with other collision systems.

Every data table can contain inconsistencies, and they can be made more apparent when considering additional functions and missing values. In this context, data tables with functional dependencies and null values represent a specific and interesting case that has been given little attention in the existing literature. This paper aims to fill this void by presenting a comprehensive framework for identifying and resolving inconsistencies in data tables that can include null values and are governed by functional dependencies. This framework is not intended to be a comprehensive solution but rather a starting point for further exploration and refinement. We have applied and expanded upon this framework to incorporate previous work, specifically in regards to repairing data tables with inconsistencies, and have made the resulting approach available for public use.

This study presents a novel dynamic econometric model, dubbed TV-PAR for short, which extends the autoregressive components of a Poisson autoregressive model to account for time-varying parameters and includes an innovation term that complies with the negative binomial distribution. TV-PAR models can be viewed as a progression of time-varying parametric Poisson autoregressive models, achieved through the inclusion of an exogenous variable that adheres to a specific distribution, allowing for Bayesian estimation methods to be applied. Furthermore, TV-PAR models can be modified to accommodate changes in parameters by employing Bayesian approaches to handle various types of data, including data with abrupt changes, data with gradual changes, and data with unspecified changes, as well as data with external driving factors.

We've observed that robots employing object-based manipulation methods often rely on explicit 3D models of objects, which can limit their ability to generalize to novel situations and new objects. In response, we've developed a novel technique where we represent objects as simple descriptors learned through contrastive training, and combine these descriptors with neural network-based value functions to anticipate the outcomes of manipulation actions. This novel framework, which we've termed Neural Descriptor Fields, ensures that object representations remain invariant under changes in orientation, position, and scaling, and it can be trained without reliance on 3D reconstruction methods or extensive datasets of manipulated objects. When applied to both synthetic and real-world manipulation scenarios, Neural Descriptor Fields exhibit a significant improvement in performance over baseline methods and a robust capacity to generalize to novel situations and new objects.

Using the functional renormalization group at the next-to-leading order in the derivative expansion, we have updated the position of the Yang-Lee edge singularity for O(N) universality classes in classic scenarios. Specifically for QCD's relevant universality classes in three dimensions, we have determined $|z_c|/R_\chi^{1/\gamma}$ to be approximately 1.607, 1.589 for $N=2, 4$ respectively. Alternatively, we have previously found $|z_c|$ to be around 2.03, 1.68 for $N=2, 4$ although these values have a more significant uncertainty.

In statistics and machine learning, it is frequently essential to establish whether a basic optimization method on a non-convex function can eventually enter a region where the function becomes locally convex. To address this, we developed an inequality that enables us to analyze the properties of the optimization landscape surrounding the solutions produced by an approximate message passing (AMP) algorithm. Specifically, we applied our inequality to demonstrate the local convexity of a particular TAP free energy function, which is relevant to the Z2 synchronization problem and the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model. Additionally, our inequality led to a confirmation of a previous conjecture regarding the efficiency of a sampling algorithm in the "easy" regime of these models.

While using photometry from stars to monitor the atmosphere may seem like an unusual approach, this method has shown promise in detecting aerosol changes, especially in the Amazon region, using observations from the MAIA mission, and in Sri Lanka, using the ATom campaign and the GPM/DPR satellite. This technique has several advantages, including being able to provide continuous information at a global scale, with the potential to supplement existing methods for monitoring aerosols using satellite data. This strategy has been applied to detect the impact of wildfires on aerosol levels, and it's also been used to analyze the effect of Asian wind patterns in carrying aerosols to Sri Lanka, which was previously unobservable with satellite data.

Recently, estimating a 6D object pose using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) has gained significant interest, with projectors and correspondences being a prominent approach. Studies have shown that using projectors alone or correspondences alone can lead to better performance than other methods, but using both together can result in a significant boost in estimated pose accuracy. To further enhance this, we present an end-to-end architecture called DeepHMap++ that combines projection grouping and correspondence learning for an estimation of 6D object pose. In the projection grouping module, a simple yet efficient non-maximum suppression technique is applied to reduce projectors, while the correspondence learning module uses a contrastive loss function to establish correspondences between feature points on the object image and the 3D object model. We pretrain our model on the LS3D dataset and conduct experiments on the COCO-6D and LPD dataset, with results showing that DeepHMap++ achieves a 6D CM score of 8.5% on the COCO-6D dataset and 11.6% on the LPD dataset, surpassing the current state-of-the-art performance.

We present GGLasso, a Python library designed to address General Graphical Lasso
challenges. Based on the original work of Friedman (2007), Graphical Lasso
estimates a sparsely constructed inverse covariance matrix $\Theta$ from
multivariate Gaussian data $\mathcal{X}$, initially introduced by Dempster (1972)
under Covariance Selection. The framework has been expanded to accommodate
hidden variables in Chandrasekaran (2012) and can be formulated as an L1-L0
optimization problem, an NP-hard issue that can be tackled via various
approximations, including L1-L1 and L1-L2 relaxation and entropic penalty methods.

Numerous numerical methods for resolving stochastic differential equations in molecular dynamics simulations have been scrutinized and assessed, focusing on deterministic impulses, drifts, and Brownian motions. By utilizing the Baker-Campbell-Hausdorff expansion, previous studies established links between methods and the underlying equations. This work extends and updates these relationships to higher order configurations and employs the results to analyze two configurational integrals related to the Nose-Hoover-Chandler method. A previously unreported expansion in the noise parameter helps characterize the accuracy of configurational sampling methods. This analysis also yields an explicit and efficient path configurational integral expression. To enhance the efficiency of sampling, the authors propose a novel method based on the analysis of configurational integrals and demonstrate its effectiveness in simulations.

Our new method calculates a variation of eigenvector centrality for multi-layered networks that incorporate node importance across different layers. In these networks, defined by separate interconnected graphs without connections between different layers, the value of a node's centrality is determined by the sum of the values of the connected nodes within each specific layer, similar to traditional eigenvector centrality calculations. Unlike standard approaches, our approach takes into account the relationships between different network layers and their respective impact on the centrality values. Unlike current multi-layer eigenvector centrality frameworks that account for inter-layer connections, our approach uses a separate set of equations that can be solved using a hybrid algorithm.

Recently, we generated the $R$-Poincar\'e algebra using deformed Poisson brackets, 
which effectively replicate the Fock coordinate transformation. This transformation 
corresponds to a de Sitter spacetime. In this study, we formulate the Dirac equation within 
$R$-Minkowski spacetime and establish that it is analogous to the Dirac equation defined 
within the de Sitter spacetime, described by its conformally flat metric. We then propose 
a novel strategy to solve the Dirac equation within the de Sitter spacetime by adopting 
the Schr\"{o}dinger picture.

This study investigates how spheres interact with water upon impact, specifically the process known as surface seal that occurs as the sphere enters the water's surface. This surface seal regime, found between low and high-speed impact velocities, features a distinctive "splash dome" formation. Empirical rules describing the transition between this seal regime and other impact behaviors have been established for both sub- and super-critical velocity conditions. However, no previous studies have been conducted at intermediate velocities, making this speed range the focus of the current research. High-speed imaging technology was utilized to capture detailed images of spheres entering water at various intermediate velocity ranges, from 0.25 to 2.5 m/s. The resulting data reveal the intricate patterns of water displacement, the formation of the splash dome, and the influence of drag on the surface seal behavior. Furthermore, the empirical rules governing the transition from the surface seal regime to other water entry behaviors have been validated in their original form in this study, with modifications also being proposed for the application to spherical objects at different velocity ranges.

A well-known issue with effective field theories is the risk of over-counting vacuua when global symmetries are present, as the concept of a global symmetry is only well-defined in the limit of infinite cutoff. This problem arises in certain Type IIB effective field theories, specifically in the context of axion-like fields, which give rise to $\theta$-terms in the effective action and result in an infinite number of vacua separated by an energy proportional to the cutoff. This distinction between the behavior of "massless" axion-like fields and true massless fields can be utilized to address the over-counting of vacua in effective field theories. This analysis is particularly relevant when analyzing the behavior of the IIB string theory at infinite energy scales, where the effective field theory description becomes inadequate and an analysis of the AdS "no-ethereiality" theorem is required. This paper also discusses the effective field theory formulation of the IIB string theory in the vicinity of a Calabi-Yau horizon, another scenario where the behavior of the theory is influenced by the presence of an infinite number of vacua, and an analysis is performed of the relevant operators and their properties in this regime.

Our calculations using first-principles methods reveal that cubanite exhibits unusual orbital selectivity, with electrons occupying certain molecular orbitals while being localized in other atomic ones. This phenomenon is exceptionally rare in 3d transition metal compounds, providing a theoretical basis for the experimentally observed lack of charge disproportionation, anomalous Mössbauer spectra, and ferromagnetic coupling between adjacent iron ions.

Recently, a remarkable achievement has been reported where two distinct dark states of excitons, located in the Hilbert space, were connected through Rabi ripples, potentially paving the way for controlled quantum transfers. Here we discuss a related but distinct approach, utilizing a single dark state and a coherent light source, to achieve massive quantum entanglement and state transfer between two distant dark excitons without the use of external magnetic fields. By utilizing a combination of theoretical modeling and numerical simulations based on experimental parameters, we demonstrate this concept's feasibility and efficiency, achieving a record for the longest-known dark exciton transfer distance of 53 nm. Additionally, we propose a method to enhance transfer distances by an order of magnitude through the incorporation of nearby acceptor impurities without compromising the initial's coherence's longevity.

Our investigation focuses on a 2D electronic lattice from a non-symmorphic wallpaper group, which is part of a larger 3D non-symmorphic crystal lattice and incorporates a translation component along one of its base vectors. By applying external pressure in a specific direction, we modified the lattice to change from a hexagonal structure to a rectangular one, thereby creating a 2D 'honeycomb2' lattice similar to graphene's lattice structure. Our study reveals that this 'honeycomb2' lattice maintains the same spatial symmetry as a hexagonal lattice and meets the necessary criteria to possess Dirac points at specific points in the Brillouin zone. Notably, we discovered that this 'honeycomb2' lattice can exhibit both topologically isolated Dirac points and a quadratic cone at the same point in the Brillouin zone by adjusting the magnitude of the atomic spin-orbit coupling relative to a specific energy range.

Quantum states known as single-photon catalyzed coherent states (SPCCSs) can be generated via quantum-optical catalysis using beam splitters or parametric amplifiers. These states occur when a coherent state and a single-photon state interact in two input ports, and a click is detected in one of them. Depending on the type of interferometer, there are different conditions that must be met in order to confidently identify the presence of a single photon, and thus successfully create SPCCSs. We have investigated the conditions under which SPCCSs can be generated using beam splitters and identify the relationship between the state fidelity and the reflection coefficient, coefficient of entanglement, and the number of photons. We have also examined the relationship between the cat-state parameter and the coherence time, and have found that SPCCSs with large cat-state parameters can be generated through interaction with a cavity of a certain type, but this comes at the cost of a shorter coherence time. We have proposed a method for generating SPCCSs using a specific type of parametric amplifier, and have examined the relationship between the state fidelity and the reflection coefficient, as well as the relationship between the cat-state parameter and the coherence time, both in the case where the number of photons is small and in the case where the number of photons is large. We have also examined the relationship between the state fidelity and the cat-state parameter in both cases.

In General Relativity using the Newman-Penrose formalism, the use of bivectors plays a key role in identifying the precise solutions to Einstein's field equations. This review focuses on explaining the fundamental principles and detailed calculations of bivectors within the Newman-Penrose formalism, specifically by converting a complex self-dual electromagnetic field from the standard Minkowski space basis to the complex null tetrad basis. As a result, we derive the complex coefficients of the Weyl tensor in the context of Newman-Penrose formalism.

A recent framework combining artificial neural networks and mixed integer linear programming for designing chemical compounds has been built upon to create a new method for polymer inference. This new method incorporates a unique way of depicting polymers using monomers, new descriptors that capture their structure, and employs linear regression in the prediction framework. Aspects of this method, such as polymer depiction and new descriptors, can be used for inferences outside of polymer context. The proposed method has been put through experimental trials using descriptors and chemical data previously established, and the results indicate it can efficiently design compounds matching given properties. The method has been applied to infer compounds with specific functional groups on polymers, demonstrating its capabilities in this area.

Identifying tumors in the esophagus from CT scans can be very difficult for humans and computer systems alike, but it's a crucial step for guiding biopsies and surgical procedures. To enhance the accuracy of this process, a new method has been developed which focuses on extracting valuable features from a limited set of scans that include biopsy marks, and has achieved the best results reported so far on two publicly available datasets. The proposed technique employs an innovative use of dense attention and dense connections to prioritize important image regions and combine features from different scales, and when compared to existing approaches has shown a significant improvement of 8.19% in terms of Dice score and 10.14% in terms of 90th percentile of histogram-based binary overlap when applied to a small dataset of 50 scans, and an even greater improvement of 11.19% and 13.15% respectively when applied to a larger dataset of 200 scans.

Multilingual individuals possess a high level of proficiency in two or more languages, enabling effective written and oral communication across multiple languages. When communicating, they may blend languages, also known as code-switching or code-mixing, by switching between different languages within a single utterance. This research explores current NLP developments, constraints, and potential obstacles in tackling five critical issues affecting multilingual communities: crisis management, healthcare, election campaigns, fake news dissemination, and hate speech. To move forward, the study proposes novel datasets and two promising approaches: transfer learning and neural machine translation. Through code-mixed challenge prototypes, researchers aim to encourage the development of suitable models and algorithms to tackle real-world problems faced by multilingual societies, applying code-mixed NLP successfully.

Tantalum oxide compounds, with the formula Ta$_2$O$_5$, are distinguished by unique properties such as high dielectric values, low loss, and chemical stability, making them suitable for applications in electronic and photonic components. However, the presence of five oxygen atoms in its molecular structure creates a challenge, leading to various configurations such as one-dimensional chains, layers, and three-dimensional structures, which can further be categorized into different classifications based on oxygen bonding patterns. To determine the most stable structure, researchers have used and combined methods from density functional theory and Monte Carlo simulations to evaluate and compare various configurations, with the goal of identifying the most stable structure at both ambient conditions and higher temperatures, with corresponding phonon spectra for validation.

Previous studies attributed online misinformation dissemination to personal factors, such as information literacy, and social media influences, but neglected a third aspect: the impact of the physical separation of Americans in geographical regions. We examined the relationship between misinformation sharing and the Big Sort, a phenomenon where communities are becoming increasingly homogeneous by physically separating people of different ages, incomes, and ideologies, based on data from Reddit forums from 2007 to 2017. We discovered that the spread of misinformation is more prevalent in homogeneous areas, although it is also significantly correlated with factors such as population density and urbanization. In addition, we found that the effect of the Big Sort is more noticeable in areas with lower population densities, and it has a greater impact on the dissemination of true versus false news articles. We propose that the Big Sort contributes to the dissemination of misinformation by reducing social connections between people from different backgrounds, leading to the reinforcement of isolated news consumption habits and the circulation of local misinformation.

Humans employ spoken language to efficiently teach other people various skills. Although robotic demonstrations are a natural teaching method, the way humans describe them through speech has not been thoroughly examined. This study investigates the way humans use speech to describe robotic demonstrations by analyzing the acoustic characteristics of their utterances. An earlier developed model of how humans use speech to describe actions was the basis for our analysis, which consisted of three components: a description of the actions' semantic features, the production mechanisms of speech, and the auditory perception of these utterances by the listeners. We applied each component of the model to explain the acoustic characteristics of the speech used in demonstrations. Twenty-four participants were asked to guide a robotic arm through three different tasks while explaining their actions verbally. The analysis of their recorded speech was then compared to data from the model, which provided a statistical representation of the acoustic features. Our results showed that the production mechanisms of speech, specifically the articulation and prosody, played a significant role in the acoustic characteristics of the utterances. Furthermore, we discovered correlations between the semantic features of the actions and certain acoustic characteristics of the utterances. These findings have implications for the development of speech-enabled teaching robots and provide a framework for predicting the acoustic characteristics of utterances that describe actions.

Quantum field theory complexity is particularly hard to define, especially when transitioning beyond simple free models in higher-dimensional spaces. A promising approach to address this difficulty is through the study of conformal field theories in (1, d) dimensions, specifically focusing on the trade-off between entanglement contribution and a measure of geometric distance. A key insight from (1, d) dimensions reveals that a class of complexity measures, which incorporate a metric structure, can be linked to a specific conformal anomaly. Building on this connection, we develop a general framework for calculating complexity in (1, d) dimensions and extend it to higher-dimensional spaces. In doing so, we enrich the Euler-Arnold equation family by introducing a new member, the Euler-Arnold-Wennberg equation. Wenberg reformulated the Euler-Arnold equation in (1, d) dimensions, providing an alternative perspective on the relationship between complexity and a conformal anomaly.

Conversational interfaces are becoming ubiquitous, and systems with these interfaces are being widely used in various settings by many individuals. Although they have achieved considerable success, the infrastructure for automated testing of these systems lags behind traditional software systems. To enhance the quality of conversational systems, developers require a robust automated testing framework that streamlines the process of crafting, executing, and updating test cases. This paper presents an automated testing framework specifically designed for conversational agents in Python, along with a micro-manager architecture that can be used to integrate the testing framework into the development of conversational agents. A case study involving this testing framework is presented, and its performance is evaluated in a controlled environment.

Cross-domain recommendations are becoming increasingly common in today's interconnected digital world.  I'm painting a picture where a user from Yahoo Mail wants to make a purchase on Amazon, but Amazon lacks the necessary information to make an informed decision.  To address this challenge, a team of researchers proposed a novel method for enhancing cross-domain recommendations that takes into account the user's preferences in multiple domains.  To better understand this concept, let's break it down into its individual components.  First, they established a strong foundation by using the theory of multi-task learning to develop a cross-domain recommendation model.  To improve this foundation, they employed the theory of meta-learning to create a flexible model that can easily switch between domains.  To further refine this model, they used the theory of graph learning to integrate the domain-specific information into the model.  To validate their approach, they conducted experiments on real-world data from multiple domains, and the results showed that their method outperformed the current state-of-the-art methods in various metrics.

Convex optimization issues often take on a more manageable form when represented with conic formulations that leverage a wide variety of exotic cones. Exotic cones in this context, refer to specialized geometric shapes with properties enabling efficient implementation of computational tools, specifically barrier oracles for their own and dual shapes. This work introduces Hypatia, an interior-point solver designed to handle these complex shapes with ease. Developed using Julia and interfacing with JuMP, Hypatia can utilize a wide assortment of predefined exotic cones. It then generates simplified equivalent formulations for various optimization applications that can provide significant improvements in processing speed and memory usage. The proposed method demonstrates a marked improvement in problem-solving efficiency when compared to more conventional and complex conic formulations.

The escalating quantity of MRI data necessitates automated quality control to ensure reliable and efficient analysis, especially in large-scale neuroimaging studies. Several approaches have been explored to develop robust and versatile MRI quality assessment methods, with a growing emphasis on machine learning techniques. However, the risk of biased models limits their generalizability to unfamiliar datasets. This study involves over 13,000 brain MRI scans from three cohorts to investigate the factors influencing the placement of abnormal samples and to develop a predictive framework for guiding future studies. The results indicate that, based on data from The Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative, the most critical factors influencing the classification of MRI scans as normal or abnormal are linked to acquisition protocols rather than individual characteristics. A decision-making theory was utilized to weight these factors and a machine learning-based classifier was trained to predict the placement of abnormal samples as new studies may recruit individuals with specific MRI scan characteristics. The study demonstrates that, based on The Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative data, models trained on cohorts with rigorous inclusion criteria struggle to generalize to cohorts with more lenient criteria, with an estimated 0.2 to 0.3 chance of correctly classifying abnormal samples as such even in more lenient cohorts. The findings and tools developed in this study can be applied to guide the design of future studies and increase the generalizability of MRI quality assessment models.

To understand how private electric vehicles influence the recovery of power grids following outages, we developed a mathematical framework that incorporates decentralized decision-making in both transportation and energy systems. We utilized multi-agent optimization to model this process and overcame computational challenges through an efficient algorithm based on precise reformation. Numerical analysis was conducted to demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach and yielded valuable policy insights, including the optimal pricing mechanisms needed to maximize grid recovery efficiency and the effects of private electric vehicles on social welfare and grid recovery duration.

The Motivation Dynamics framework, a concept explored in recent studies that applies bifurcations to model an autonomous agent's decision-making processes, is further developed to accommodate multiple autonomous entities in this paper. We demonstrate how the framework's capabilities can be expanded to capture persistent, cooperative behavior between agents meeting at specific locations, and through in-depth analysis and numerical data, reveal that this extension exhibits a complex pattern indicative of a strange attractor.

We investigated the structural, electronic, and magnetic properties of GdSn3, CmSn3, and the series GdxCm1-xSn3 ($x = 0.25, 0.5, 0.75$) using the full potential linearized augmented plane wave method within the generalized gradient approximation+U. We calculated the lattice parameters, binding energies, and magnetic moments for all three materials. The results show that the lattice parameters of GdSn3 and CmSn3 differ significantly due to the large difference in atomic radii of their constituent elements. However, the binding energies and magnetic moments of the two compounds are very similar. The phase transitions and binding energy variations along the [001] and [110] directions were also examined using the frozen phonon method. The results indicate that both GdSn3 and CmSn3 undergo structural transformations from the CaF3 to the PbCl3 phase type. The calculations also revealed that the CmSn3 compound exhibits a more complex antiferromagnetic arrangement of its spins. The magnetic moments of the Sn atoms in both GdSn3 and CmSn3 were found to be non-zero, indicating that the Sn atoms contribute to the magnetic properties of the compounds. The calculations further showed that the GdxCm1-xSn3 series exhibits the coexistence of GdSn3 and CmSn3 properties, with the CmSn3 component prevailing at the x = 0

The paper reviews predictions made by an extension of the standard model called the bilepton model, which involves changing the electroweak symmetry from $SU(2)\times U(1)$ to $SU(3)\times U(1)$, and includes three types of bileptons: lepton-lepton, lepton-neutrino, and lepton-quark interactions. Although the bilepton model has similar characteristics to the $SU(3)\times U(1)$ gauge model, it was originally proposed to resolve the baryon asymmetry problem, it can also predict additional baryon and meson particles, which can be experimentally verified through high-energy scattering experiments, such as those that occur at the Tevatron, LHC, or future colliders like ILC or CERN's future upgrade, which could provide evidence for the model's validity.

The concept of a basis, specifically in relation to finite Coxeter groups of type B, has been well established through the work of M. W. Davis. According to his findings, a subset of a basis can be designated as a basis if and only if it contains no fewer than n-1 elements and satisfies the condition that each remaining generator can be expressed as a product of exactly two elements from the subset, with an even number of sign changes when applied to the invariant polynomial. Our study extends this criterion to determine which subsets of a basis are also a basis, for n distinct labels, by reinterpreting the condition in terms of the invariant polynomial's roots.

Utilizing the Pantheon SN Ia dataset and Sloan Digital Sky Survey, we've developed a method to calculate weak lensing convergence by combining data on the positions and photometry of foreground galaxies. A correlation between this approach and the residual Hubble diagram values of Type Ia supernovae holds a $3.6\sigma$ significance and is consistent with dark matter effects due to galactic halos. Furthermore, we constrained galactic halo properties, including the mass-to-light ratio $\Gamma$ and the radial distribution of matter density $\rho(r)$, with $\rho(r)$ approximated as a Navarro-Frenk-Shaken profile, with results indicating $\rho(r)$ peaks at $r_200$ with $\rho_{200}=(1.13^{+0.38}_{-0.33})\rho_{\rm crit}$ and $\Gamma=(13.8^{+5.0}_{-4.2})$ with associated uncertainties.

The development of efficient and controllable quantum communication networks will depend heavily on the creation of reliable interfaces for coupling optical signals with qubits. Optical centres in silicon have shown great promise in this area, with one type of defect, known as T centres, exhibiting a strong optical interaction with a fundamental mode of a photonic crystal nanocavity. Although previously studied, the optical properties of T centres in silicon remain poorly understood, and previous research has mainly been based on outdated interpretations of data. In the course of this study, a re-examination of existing knowledge about T centres was conducted, accompanied by the collection of fresh data from cavity-enhanced Raman spectroscopy and a theoretical analysis of their optical characteristics. The results were used to re-evaluate the earlier findings and provided the basis for a discussion on the distinction between T centres and other silicon defects, as well as on potential paths for further investigation.

For our task that considers context, a suitable object detector is needed.
We examine two popular object detectors, a fully convolutional network and a U-Net,
and evaluate their performance using both a custom dataset and images from the COCO dataset.
Our results show that neither of these detectors prioritizes the context over the focal point,
either based on distance or on segmentation mask overlap.
We also investigate the influence of the context on object detection for various scenarios
and find that in many cases, the context does not play a significant role.
Our context-free dataset can be used by other researchers to explore this topic further.

We provide a new framework for a broad range of binary random variables that depend negatively, including functions of independent Bernoulli trials and exchangeable binary sequences. Within this framework, we establish concentration inequalities for a broad range of functions of these variables, including a submartingale inequality for a specific arrangement and an entropy inequality for random variables conditioned on an event. These inequalities can be applied to derive a wide range of consequences, such as moment bounds, large deviations, and an Efron-Stein decomposition for functions of these variables. We also discuss the relationship between our approach and existing methods for negatively dependent random variables.

Wilberd van der Kallen translated this 1951 thesis into English, originally written by T.A. Springer. Springer investigated the method of categorizing conjugacy classes within the symplectic group Sp_n(K), specifically focusing on fields K with a characteristic other than two. His work revealed that each conjugacy class can be distinguished using a combination of invariant characteristics. These characteristics initially mirror those found in the general linear group – namely, irreducible polynomials and systems of non-negative integers in a 0-to-n+1 range – and then incorporate additional features related to the symmetric and alternating groups Al_n and Sl_n derived from Immanuel Kantor's construction.

A key challenge in kidney transplants arises from incompatibilities between donors and patients, which has been exacerbated by the growing scarcity of kidney donors. Desensitization techniques, such as plasma exchange and immunosuppressive drugs, have been developed to make incompatibilities more compatible, but they are expensive, complicated, and sometimes ineffective, and as such, should be used judiciously. A crucial step in using these techniques wisely is determining which incompatibilities they should be applied to. This problem falls under the broader category of ranking problems, which can be resolved using multiple attribute ranking, a method originally developed for evaluating airline safety. This paper reinterprets multiple attribute ranking to address the issue of prioritizing incompatible kidney transplants, with the aim of developing an optimal strategy for applying desensitization techniques. It achieves this by formulating the problem as an integer linear programming problem that can be solved efficiently. This paper performs a comprehensive mathematical examination of the correlation
between two prominent word embedding models, FastText and Word2Vec, and a well
known text polarity metric, the Loughran-McDonald polarity measure. The study
analyzes the connection between the geometric representation of embedded words and
their corresponding classification labels, employing the concept of angle measures
to quantify the relationship. A novel calculation is introduced to estimate the
standard deviation of embedded words, allowing for the construction of a normal
distribution that represents the distribution of embedded words. This distribution
is then utilized to compute the probability of word pairs being correctly classified
as having the same or different polarities. The analysis is performed on a large
newspaper dataset, utilizing both Word2Vec and FastText, and the results show
that the probability of correct classification varies significantly, with values as
low as 0.75 for the most extreme word pairs. The study also examines the relationship
between word embedding dimensions and the accuracy of classification, showing that
the accuracy does not necessarily increase with more embedding dimensions. The
results have important implications for utilizing word embeddings in classification
tasks, highlighting the importance of rigorous testing and validation. The study
concludes by suggesting the use of a threshold on the cosine similarity distance
to define the relationship between word pairs, providing a foundation for future
research on the topic.

This article presents the SISO-OFDM and MISO-OFDM based IDET systems as alternatives to our previously proposed optimal wideband waveforming strategy in [1].
Fair-throughput and sum-throughput optimisation problems are defined and formulated.
By leveraging an algorithm that utilizes fixed points, we derive the optimal fair-throughput and sum-throughput values for SISO-OFDM and MISO-OFDM systems.

This research introduces a new method to model the interaction of fluids with changing phases, combining level-set and embedded boundary techniques. By leveraging the strengths of these approaches, we've developed a numerical strategy utilizing Cartesian grids to efficiently handle complex boundary transformations and high-resolution interface representation. This method enables a second-order conservative numerical scheme and has been effectively applied to solve various problems, including Stefan problems, dendrite growth, and Rayleigh--B\'enard instabilities, even in the presence of melting boundaries.

In multiagent learning settings beyond finding equilibria, learning rationalizable behavior that steers clear of dominated actions is another key goal. This work is the first to explore how learning algorithms can be designed to discover rationalizable equilibria in multiagent games by utilizing the logical connection between rationalizable behavior and Nash equilibria. A key innovation here is the development of an efficient algorithm to determine whether a given Nash equilibrium is rationalizable, which in turn is used in a second algorithm to discover all rationalizable equilibria in multiagent games. Both of these algorithms are guaranteed to yield correct results in a variety of game formats, and the time they take to do so is bounded by specific polynomial functions of the number of players and actions in the game. A novel aspect of this work is the introduction of a new class of games called "rationalizable-over-Nash" (RON games, which are distinguished by the property that every Nash equilibrium contains a subset of rationalizable actions, and in such games it is proven that all rationalizable equilibria can be discovered using a variant of the \epsilon-Nash mixed equilibrium finding algorithm. A key result related to RON games is that they include a subclass of games identified as "rationalizable-in-mixed-strategies" (RMS games, which are distinguished by the property that every mixed strategy that makes every player act rationally is also a Nash equilibrium, and in RMS games the number of rationalizable actions is proven to be bounded

An analysis of a stochastic Susceptible to Infective to Recovered model is conducted, where the model is based on an Erdős-Rényi random graph that changes dynamically as susceptible individuals connected to infected neighbours form new connections or sever existing ones. As the model is scaled to accommodate large populations, researchers obtained mathematical proofs of key properties of the model, particularly its early stages and the behaviour of its epidemic threshold. They also demonstrated that below this threshold the model exhibits random fluctuations, while above it the model experiences an abrupt shift towards a different dynamic. The study of this model reveals interesting contrasts to a similar model based on a random regular graph of a fixed degree, where the model exhibits no phase transition even when scaled to accommodate large populations.

Integrating diverse datasets, stemming from data and theoretical sources, is a crucial yet challenging task in data analysis, particularly when performing fits for model parameters. While aligning the format of experimental data is a straightforward process, reconciling disparate theoretical predictions is a more complex process with many obstacles to overcome. In the context of particle physics, predicting cross-sections or other properties involves multiple calculations, each performed by different individuals or groups, with their own methods and assumptions, and are often based on different models and models' parameters, as seen in the case of proton structure function predictions. In this work, we outline a general framework for integrating such sources, with a focus on proton structure functions, and demonstrate the application of this framework by incorporating Higgs boson cross-section predictions into the PDF fitting framework for the Tevatron, a process that is otherwise infeasible due to the computational demands of these calculations.

To accelerate policy optimization in complex, dynamic environments with multiple variables, reinforcement learning agents can effectively utilize previously collected, historical data. Standard experience replay enables agents to retain information from prior iterations. However, the current method equally values all collected observations, neglecting their varying significance. A more adaptive approach, the variance reduction based experience replay framework, selectively leverages the most informative historical data. This approach prioritizes visits that are likely to lead to optimal policies, as well as those associated with a higher variance in return values, in order to accelerate exploration and optimization, and reduce the gap between the current policy and the optimal policy. By adjusting the weights of these terms, the agent can efficiently optimize the variance of return values, thus obtaining an improved policy. We theoretically and experimentally validate the efficacy of this simple and effective method, demonstrating its capability to accelerate policy optimization in both static and dynamic environments.

In our analysis of conversational dialogue, we encounter various branching scenarios, in which a single question can lead to multiple possible responses, and different responses can yield distinct and sometimes contradictory continuations. To effectively grasp dialogue structures, a model must excel at capturing these complex relationships across multiple branches. To challenge state-of-the-art models in this regard and provide a platform for research on high-branching dialogue tasks, we present MultiTalk, a massive conversational dataset comprising over 32 million turns of branching dialogue. In our experiments using models fine-tuned on large language datasets, we found that both T5 and t5-tx achieve significant improvements over existing approaches in generating coherent continuations, especially in predicting subsequent branches. Nonetheless, there is room for further advancement, as their performance falls short of human capabilities in certain instances. With its expansive size and intricate branch patterns, MultiTalk offers valuable insights and presents opportunities for innovation in modeling high-branching dialogue, as well as guidelines for simplifying the task, which can be useful for assessing models like BART and T0.

We introduce MG-GLAM, a computational tool developed to rapidly create comprehensive N-body simulations for various cosmological theories, specifically modified gravity models. This program builds upon the existing GLAM code and incorporates an advanced multigrid method to solve the non-linear equations characteristic of modified gravity theories, resulting in highly efficient simulations. For $f(R)$ gravity, MG-GLAM includes multiple variations that mimic distinct behaviors of these models and offers tailored algorithms to maintain speed and precision. The code excels at producing a broad spectrum of modified gravity simulations and offers significant computational benefits, outperforming existing N-body simulations by as much as 10 times while achieving realistic cosmic large-scale structure on less than 10^6 cubic megaparsecs.

Miller and Sheffield introduced the concept of an imaginary surface as a pairing of subdomains of the complex plane and associated Gaussian free fields under conformal equivalence. Specifically, they considered the relationship between these pairings and chordal Schramm-Loewner evolution. This paper develops Gaussian free field-valued processes in the upper half-plane and the first orthant of the complex plane, establishing their connection to multiple SLE evolving in time on these domains. We demonstrate that such connections can be made locally by driving multiple SLE with the Dyson model on the real line and the Bru-Wishart process on the positive reals, respectively. Ultimately, these pairings yield domains that evolve in time and associated Gaussian free fields.

MediaWiki's 'WorkingWiki' is an open-source extension that converts a wiki
into a sophisticated collaborative platform for developing high-quality manuscripts
and software projects. Originally developed at McMaster University's theoretical
biology lab, WorkingWiki enables multiple users to work together on a range of
tasks by utilizing command-line tools to translate raw 'drafts' into polished projects.
Its features include automatic citation and reference checking, syntax and style
verification, and advanced code compilation, among others. By integrating numerous
tools and features into the wiki environment, WorkingWiki minimizes the need to
switch between different applications, thereby boosting productivity and reducing
errors. This paper details the architecture, customization options, and features
of WorkingWiki, which is compatible with a wide range of projects and can be used
with Mediawiki versions 1.31 to 1.35. By providing pre-configured 'drafts,' or'starter
kits,' developers can easily set up their own WorkingWiki project. As an open-source
project, WorkingWiki is designed to be highly adaptable and customizable to meet
the diverse needs of its users.

A nonlinear model, specifically an active flame model, has been applied to analyze the dynamics of a turbulent jet flame. The model, which incorporates reaction rates influenced by flame temperature and a flame surface area-based description, has been linearized to examine flame response in a low-amplitude acoustic field. The results from the linear model were then compared to actual measurements of a jet flame subject to acoustic forcing. The study demonstrated that the reaction rate reaction rate response could be described using the passive response of the jet, whereas the temperature response could be explained by the distribution of flame surface area. Furthermore, the study found that the flame response could be accurately predicted using a model that accounted for flame surface area and included a preference for flame response near natural instability, even in the absence of acoustic forcing. The linear model showed limited improvement over the simple model based on flame surface area, yet it was found to overpredict the response of the jet flame in certain situations, likely due to the influence of heat loss and the role of hydrodynamics on the reaction rates.

We investigate the neutrinoless double beta decay driven by an extremely light dark matter field interacting with neutrinos, particularly focusing on the impact when this interaction breaches lepton number, which directly leads to a significant significance for cosmological parameters, specifically the Hubble constant and effective neutrino density, and also affects the relic abundance of dark matter. The condition under which the neutrinoless double beta decay signal becomes noticeable can be determined by considering the interplay between an ongoing experiment's sensitivity and cosmological parameters, and we find that future cosmological surveys will easily detect this relation, allowing for the relic abundance of dark matter to be determined with great precision, and also allowing for a direct determination of the neutrinoless double beta decay amplitude by looking at this abundance in the presence of a detection of the decay. Additionally, we examine the possibility that neutrinoless double beta decay could be caused by an interaction between dark matter and neutrinos that is mediated by a light pseudoscalar, which could be directly confirmed through observations of the 7.3 GHz line, and also has implications for the evolution of the cosmic microwave background, specifically modifying the breakdown of temperatures equilibration in the early universe.

Nonlocal gravity theory is a classical generalization of Einstein's gravity theory. Based on an analogy with nonlocal electrodynamics, this new model involves a history-dependent relation that can be confirmed through data. The purpose of this paper is to modify nonlocal gravity theory so that the nonlocal aspect relates directly to observable properties, similar to the approach in nonlocal electrodynamics. The reformulated theory results in a constitutive relation identical to one proposed recently by Puetzfeld, Obukhov, and Hehl. The nonlocal gravity theory can be applied to show that de Sitter spacetime does not meet the theory's requirements.

Understanding how genomic elements affect specific traits through genome-wide association studies remains complex due to the sheer number of available annotations. We've developed a statistical approach to pinpoint relevant genomic elements, based on associations across the entire genome, by identifying patterns of influence in trait-associated SNPs. This method can incorporate multiple annotation types and has been successfully applied to eighteen human traits such as blood, platelet counts, metabolic disorders, and height. By combining this method with genome-wide association results and publicly available genomic data, we analyzed enrichment, pattern of influence and colocalization for these eighteen traits. Our results show that protein-coding regions, particularly those within genes associated with specific functions, influence genetic associations in various ways, with a notable prevalence of coding regions associated with metabolic disorders. Notably, the majority of trait-associated SNPs lack a clear link to nearby genes, with the exception of height, which is distinct in this regard. Our approach has been made available for public use through an online platform.

This paper discusses recent findings from the LHC involving small systems studied
by the ALICE, ATLAS and CMS collaborations. Due to the growing significance
of QCD in small systems, particularly in situations with high multiplicity, not
all pertinent research can be covered within this report. It primarily examines
measurements focusing on collective behavior in small systems and new results on
strangeness enhancement observed in proton-proton interactions. It is essential to
note that many notable findings have been excluded from the discussion presented
here.

Observations of some variable X-ray sources within the Milky Way's center that have shown no outbursts in over a decade have led some researchers to suggest a significant population of stellar mass black holes in the region. A crucial aspect of the theory that these sources are actually black holes is the claim that neutron star binaries with low masses exhibit recurring X-ray bursts within short intervals. This study contradicts that idea by revealing that about half of the known LMXBs, featuring a neutron star as the primary component, exhibit outburst recurrence times similar to those of the Galactic Center X-ray binaries, the other half having much longer intervals between outbursts. The study's method of determining recurrence times was based on the analysis of nearly a decade's worth of data from the all-sky monitor aboard NASA's Swift spacecraft, covering a time frame from 2005 to 2013. The data showed that the distribution of neutron star binaries in the galaxy with short outburst recurrence times pales in comparison to the number of the same type of binaries with longer outburst recurrence times, the ratio the two being roughly 1:4.5, the figure likely subject to change with more comprehensive data. The research also identified two known neutron star binaries with outburst recurrence times so short they should be visible in the Milky Way Center, suggesting that the population of the region may not be entirely composed of black holes.

THz radiation enables the precise stimulation of vibrational frequencies in molecules and crystals, leading to the introduction of inertial influences on electrons. By drawing a comparison to classical mechanics, where circular motion generates Coriolis and centrifugal forces, analogous effects arise, specifically spin-rotation coupling, centrifugal field coupling, and the interplay of these forces with the spin-orbit and the redshift of energy levels. These effects can persist for a few picoseconds following the initial stimulation, and potentially amplify the impact of radiation on materials at the level of atomic or molecular scales.

Improving neural conversational agents' ability to produce diverse and engaging responses in casual conversations is a challenge. To tackle this issue, this paper introduces two significant innovations. Firstly, it proposes a new metric called Natural Language Inference Diversified Response (NLI-DR), which assesses the degree of response diversity by considering the NLI semantic similarities between conversational responses. Utilizing NLI-DR, the paper identifies multiple factors contributing to response diversity, including the use of multiple conversation histories, whether the query is continued from previous ones, whether the response is conditioned on multiple conversation histories, and whether the query represents a true change. A simple yet effective approach is then developed to enhance response diversity by taking into account the degree of change in the conversation. Secondly, the paper introduces a more challenging semantic diversity dialogue task, which is met by presenting two challenging versions of the task, easy versions previously proposed by other researchers. To solve this task, the paper develops two simple yet effective models to achieve both task difficulty and neural conversational agents' response diversity goals simultaneously. Experimental evaluations on multiple datasets confirm the validity of NLI-DR and the effectiveness of the two proposed models in achieving semantic diversity in dialogue.

The occurrence of stable hydrogen burning in very low-mass stars is influenced by their rotation rates. Studies suggest that sub-stellar objects with masses similar to those of brown dwarfs and radii comparable to those of Saturn, when rotating rapidly, may experience sufficient centrifugal force to counteract the gravitational pull, leading to the formation of equatorial hydrogen-rich atmospheres. This allows hydrogen burning to continue, even if the objects' luminosities fall below a certain limit, providing an alternative explanation for the observed number of blue, hydrogen-burning dwarfs. However, the effects of rotation on density and pressure on these objects are not well understood and are difficult to model without numerical methods. Using the TOAD (Thermals And Dynamics) code, a model of rotating objects is simulated, with code modifications allowing it to efficiently handle convection and semi-grey radiative transfer. With this model, objects are simulated at a range of rotation rates and masses, with results compared to previous analytical models. The code also models objects with extreme oblateness, with results consistent with previous studies, with the added prediction that rapid rotation leads to objects with masses less than 0.25 solar masses to experience convective heat transport, with this effect becoming more pronounced at higher rotation rates. With code validation complete, the effects of rotation on the internal and external properties of sub-stellar objects are examined, with the aim of determining at what rotation rate the objects lose stable hydrogen burning capacity. The technique of amplitude analysis in hadron decay studies is very effective, 
however, relies heavily on accurate knowledge of various factors, including the 
background processes and systematic uncertainties. This paper outlines the most 
common sources of hadron decay data analysis uncertainty, including reconstruction 
methods, selection efficiency estimates, fit methods, normalisation techniques, 
and amplitude analyses. It also provides guidance on obtaining and using the necessary
datasets and calculation code for modeling hadron decay processes and calculating 
model uncertainty weights. As part of this effort, we present examples of necessary 
datasets and calculation code for specific processes and offer advice on conducting 
and presenting amplitude analysis uncertainty calculations.

A new model based on a comprehensive expression for radiation energy has been proposed, and it effectively elucidates the dynamics of afterglows in multiple contexts, including relativistic, non-relativistic phases and fireball radiations with radiative and adiabatic components.

Bipartite graphs depicting connections between distinct groups of objects have numerous practical applications, and their representation is often an essential step in various data analysis methods, including multidimensional scaling and stochastic block models. Unfortunately, verifying whether a given bipartite graph represents a specific, desired structure is generally a challenging problem that can't be solved with the current computational technology. In our research, we created an algorithm that uses branch and bound to solve this problem and has a predicted time cost that is directly proportional to a predetermined number that grows in proportion to the square of the number of groups and is also in proportion to the cube of the number of nodes in the smaller of the two groups, although this projected time cost is based on an analysis that assumes the most challenging case in which the largest group contains 99% of the total number of nodes.

Recently, researchers have successfully implemented autonomous, rugged walking capabilities in various robots, but these achievements are often achieved at the expense of other essential functions being served, such as thruster operation in bipedal robots. As a step forward, this paper explores the potential benefits of utilizing thrusters in bipedal robots by converting some of the mechanical energy from the ground into hydraulic power. A key aspect of this investigation involves re-examining the conservation of energy principle to better understand the interplay between walking and hydraulic dynamics. To validate the proposed concept, this study includes the design of a cost-effective, thruster-assisted bipedal robot and an associated control system. To enhance the efficiency of the robot's hydraulic system, researchers also developed an advanced model-based control strategy. To evaluate the thruster-assisted robot's performance, a series of outdoor experiments were conducted under various conditions, and the results showed that the robot can achieve optimal walking patterns with increased stability, efficiency, and robustness due to the aid of the thrusters and the developed control system. To facilitate the reproduction of the results, an open-source version of the robot's design and control system is made available online.

Becker-Denef-Lipschitz first observed in 1979 that over finite fields $k$, the total residue map $\text{res}$ from Laurent series to $k$ is expressible in a specific language, provided $t$ is included as a parameter. This discovery motivated further research into the properties of a specific mathematical theory related to valued fields. In the course of these investigations, the authors proved that this theory does not have a certain desirable feature and demonstrated that, for infinite fields $k$, the associated power series fields cannot be computationally decided. This, in turn, led to an analogous undecidability conclusion for a specific complex-valued field of power series.

Recent research in cryptography has focused on side-channel resistance, with an emerging interest in exploring the effectiveness of cryptographic protocols in environments where computational resources are severely limited. In the context of a specific attack, known as the "inference attack," the speed at which operations are performed is directly used to uncover private information. As a result, protocols that withstand this attack require a significant number of high-speed operations to be performed with precise timing. In our research, we aim to develop a clear and concise understanding of the relationship between the speed of operations and security in the presence of an inference attack. To this end, we propose a method for estimating the number of operations required to ensure a desired level of security, which we call the "efficiency threshold." Next, we investigate the relationship between the speed of operations and security by implementing our method using a variety of low-level programming languages and benchmarking tools. In particular, we examine the effect of reducing the frequency of a CPU or the number of operations in a cryptographic protocol on security, as well as the effectiveness of protocols that withstand the inference attack in various scenarios, by varying the effective frequency of a CPU from 1 GHz to 10 kHz. Finally, we discuss the implications of our findings for the design of side-channel resistant cryptographic protocols in the presence of an inference attack, where we suggest considering the "degrade factor" of a protocol, which represents the ratio of the actual frequency of operations to the effective frequency, as a key factor in protocol design

A localized alteration in knot diagrams is referred to as an unknotting operation. It can be demonstrated that any knot diagram can be transformed into a trivial unknot through a sequence of unknotting operations, combined with some variations in the diagram configuration, which are referred to as Reidemeister moves. Unknotting operations hold significant value in the field of knot theory; they serve a purpose in analyzing the intricacy of knots and knot-related properties. Moreover, they also have applications in the study of knot projections and configurations. In this study, a new type of unknotting operation is introduced for both classical and welded knots. It differs from the existing types of unknotting operations and new characteristics associated with it have been discovered. It has been demonstrated that the new operation can be performed using a specific type of Reidemeister move, specifically the type 3 move.
